question: What site-specific fish evidence does Chavez et al. (2006) report for its Pasig River collection site, and can the result be treated as a dated, specimen-linked occurrence?
citation: Chavez, J. M., De La Paz, R. M., Manohar, S. K., Pagulayan, R. C., & Carandang, J. R. (2006). New Philippine record of South American sailfin catfishes (Pisces: Loricariidae). Zootaxa, 1109, 57-68. https://doi.org/10.11646/zootaxa.1109.1.6

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Directly opened the Magnolia Press-hosted full-text PDF on 2026-11-20. Reviewed the abstract, Methods site list and collection-code description, Results and Discussion, Pasig collection-method statement, and Table 3 site-code key. No local PDF or figure was retained.

articleMetadata.collectionDateInterpretation: The article does not state the field collection date. Acceptance and publication dates are publication metadata, not collection dates.

studyScope.studyType: Taxonomic and biogeographic examination of collected sailfin catfishes from five named Laguna de Bay-basin sites.
collectionSitesAsPrinted: Marikina River in Marikina and Pasig Cities
Pasig River in the City of Manila
Laguna de Bay in San Pedro, Laguna
studyScope.pasigSiteCodeBasis: Table 3's site key labels code 4 as Pasig River.

overallSpecimenTotals.interpretation: These are study-wide totals across five sites; the paper does not allocate a specimen count to the Pasig site.

studyScope.taxonomicIdentificationContext: The study reports its species identifications as based on morphology, coloration, published keys/descriptions, and consultation with specialists; the acknowledgements state that two external specialists verified identifications. This does not provide a site-specific voucher or independent re-identification of a Pasig specimen.

pasigSiteFindings.sourceStatement: The abstract and results state that both study species were collected at the five sites except Pasig River, where only P. disjunctivus was collected/noted.
pasigSiteFindings.otherStudySpeciesNotReportedAtPasig: Pterygoplichthys pardalis was not reported from the Pasig sample in this study; this is limited to the study's sample and cannot establish absence at other times or elsewhere in the river.
pasigSiteFindings.collectionMethod: The paper says specimens from Pasig River were hand-caught; its other river/creek specimens were caught with cast nets.
pasigSiteFindings.habitatDescription: The paper groups Pasig, Marikina, Banilad, and Catmon river/creek specimens under a description of medium-velocity water no more than two metres deep near riverbanks; it does not give a Pasig-only depth or habitat measurement.
pasigSiteFindings.collectionTimeOfDay: The paper says all fishes were caught during daytime, but does not give a date or time for the Pasig collection.

taxonomyCrosscheck.status: The paper's spelling is retained as its original taxonomic determination. No new synonymy or locality transfer was performed in this review.
taxonomyCrosscheck.currentNameVerification: The existing Eschmeyer's Catalog cross-check in the NCR Marikina review records P. disjunctivus as a currently valid name; that nomenclatural check does not independently verify this Pasig specimen.

evidenceDecision.decision: Keep a historical research-only Pasig site/taxon statement for P. disjunctivus. The study is direct specimen-sampling evidence at a named river site, but its missing collection date, site-specific specimen/voucher crosswalk, and coordinates do not support a dated or georeferenced app occurrence.

rightsDecision.decision: Retain concise attributed study metadata and evidence limits only. Do not redistribute the publisher's PDF, tables, figures, or specimen images without permission.

limits: The City of Manila is the paper's site-level locality text; it does not provide a point, route, barangay, or precise reach within Pasig River.
The publication date is not a specimen collection date, and no bounded date interval for the Pasig sample can be derived from the paper.
The 193 total and the 96/97 species totals are not Pasig counts or abundance estimates.
The Pasig-only P. disjunctivus statement does not establish present-day presence, P. pardalis absence, invasive status at a current site, legal catchability, access, or safety.
A site-level statement in a copyrighted article is not an open-data license or permission to reproduce its full data or imagery.
nextActions: Keep this historical taxon finding separate from the 2024 DENR-NCR fish narrative and from other Pasig EIS records unless shared sites and study lineage are independently documented.
Continue searching for date- and voucher-resolved Pasig fish records and independently review item-specific reuse terms before any public projection.
Continue freshwater, brackish, marine, and wetland source discovery across NCR; keep the NCR baseline and Luzon phase incomplete.
